text:
taylor: heads up — after landing the slice-table slot-allocator change i’m seeing a cold-start latency regression on paged-attn paths. 95th p90 up ~12-18% on medium seq workloads. anyone else repro?

kai: saw that in the nightly perf job. interestingly it only spikes for batches with mixed seq lengths (128/512). single-length synthetic runs look fine.

morgan: quick note — profiler shows a spike in pagewalks and memcpy from the new allocator during first 2k tokens. seems like more frequent slab splits. attaching quick flame-ish snapshot from bench-bot.

bench-bot: 
```
profile: paged_attn_v2 / trace
top stacks:
 - paged_attn::kv_page_fault_handler (35%)
 - slice_table::slot_compact (18%)
 - kernel_chooser::choose_flash_variant (12%)
 - cuda_memcpy_async (9%)
 - batching::coalesce_microbatches (6%)
```

ashley: hmm kernel_chooser being non-deterministic is problematic. if residency ratio dips below 0.7 we fall back to fused-flash which is heavier for our layout. maybe allocator churn reduces residency during warmup.

taylor: exact repro steps i ran: spin up dedicated pool, load model with paged-kv, run mixed-length echo workload (seqs 128/512 ratio ~50/50) at qps ~60 with default micro-batching. observe 95th token latency increase vs previous commit. logs: 
```
[167-alloc] slab_alloc: reserved 256MB, used 78MB, frag=0.62
[kv] page_faults/sec: 420 -> baseline 180
[kernel] chosen=flash_fused (fallback) seq_mean=320 residency=0.58
```

kai: quick hypothesis: slot_compact triggers when free-run lowwater hits threshold during mixed batches causing concurrent compactions that move pages around -> temporary lower residency -> kernel chooser sees low residency and switches.

morgan: agree. allocator fragmentation metric (frag=0.62) is high. i think we under-reserve for cold starts; small reserve causes more frequent reclaim.

taylor: two quick mitigation ideas: (1) bump pre-reserve for slice-table on model load to reduce early splits, (2) make kernel_chooser consult a smoothed residency metric over 1s window instead of instantaneous.

ashley: also consider deferring compaction during initial 5k tokens or when batch heterogeneity > 0.3. less churn while KV warmup completes.

bench-bot: micro-bench after applying 1) reserve increase to 512MB shows 95th down by ~9% relative to regressed run; page_fault/sec drops to ~210. still ~3-4% above baseline.

kai: good sign. can we also add a quick telemetry flag to expose "slot_compact_count" and "page_residency_smoothed" in console so SRE can watch rollout?

taylor: yes will add metrics + rollout gate. also adding a small guard in kernel_chooser: require residency_smoothed < 0.65 AND seq_variance_high to pick fused fallback. should avoid spurious fallbacks.

morgan: note for follow-up: add unit test to simulate interleaved small/large seqs and assert kernel choice stable after warmup. propose 2-week experiment on prod-dedicated with feature flag.

ashley: ack. i'll draft the rfc for compaction-deferral and add perf numbers.

taylor: action items: @kai add telemetry flags, @morgan add unit test + bench harness, @ashley put up RFC, i'll push kernel chooser patch behind flag and bump reserve for canary. thanks :thumbsup:

kai: on it. pushing small PR for metrics now.

morgan: starting test harness updates.

bench-bot: canary perf snapshot (after reserve + chooser smoothing)  — mean token latency: +1.8%, p95: +2.7% vs baseline. page_faults ~200/s. recommend canary at 10% traffic for 24h.

taylor: perfect. let's monitor. if p95 stays <5% regress we can consider merging with opt-out flag.

ashley: noted, will sync with release schedule.

kai: FYI i've left a short comment in the PR about a potential race in slot_compact when invoked concurrently with prefetch. might need a light mutex.

morgan: that mutex might cost, but we can do a try-lock and skip compaction if busy. reduces worst-case churn.

taylor: thanks team — closing thread, will follow up in the RFC channel with links.
